faq.t2.label: Question 2
faq.t2.default: What is the difference between ductile iron and grey cast iron?
faq.t2.text: What is the difference between ductile iron and grey cast iron?

faq.r2.label: Answer 2
faq.r2.default: In ductile iron (also called spheroidal graphite or S.G. iron) the graphite forms round nodules, which makes the metal much stronger and far less brittle than grey cast iron, where the graphite forms flakes. A ductile iron cover can therefore be lighter for the same load class and is less likely to crack under impact. Grey cast iron is heavier for the same strength but economical, and is widely used for lighter-duty covers, gratings and agricultural rings.

loadguide.r0.label: Introduction
loadguide.r0.default:
Every manhole cover, access cover and gully grating is made for a certain load. In the UK, Europe and many export markets the load is given by a class of the standard EN 124 (in the UK: BS EN 124). The class is a letter and a number: the number is the test load in kilonewtons (kN) the cover and frame must carry without breaking. The letter stands for the place where the product may be installed.

Choosing the class is the most important decision when you specify a cover: a cover that is too light for the traffic can crack or rock; one that is far heavier than needed costs more and is harder to lift.

loadguide.t4.text: How to choose the right class

loadguide.r2.label: How to choose
loadguide.r2.default:
• Start from the place of installation, not from the vehicle: the standard gives the minimum class for each place (the groups in the table).
  • Think about what may happen later. A footway cover that cars or delivery vans may drive over needs at least C250; if lorries can reach it, choose D400.
  • Kerbside gratings sit where wheels often run: C250 is the minimum, D400 where heavy traffic is frequent.
  • Roads and car parks for all vehicles need D400. Busy or high-speed roads also need covers that do not rock and do not make noise, such as double triangular or cushioned designs.
  • Follow the project specification. When the specification and this guide differ, the specification applies. When in doubt, choose the higher class.

ai.summary: JPK Metallics Pvt. Ltd is an Indian iron foundry in Howrah, West Bengal, with its corporate office in Kolkata. Since 1976 it has made ductile iron and grey cast iron manhole covers, gratings, engineering castings, pipe fittings and agricultural castings (Cambridge rings) for customers in India, the UK, USA, Europe, the Middle East and Africa.
facts: Founded in 1976 as Shree Jagannath Ferro Casting; family-run for five decades.
Integrated 1,85,000 sq.ft. foundry at Uluberia, Howrah, West Bengal, India: melting, moulding and machining under one roof.
Two induction furnaces and two cupola furnaces with a combined melting capacity of 15,000 tonnes a year; DISA ARPA 900 and ARPA 450 moulding machines; a no-bake line for complex engineering castings.

Makes ductile iron (SG iron) and grey cast iron castings: manhole covers and frames (solid top, recessed, double triangular), gratings, tree grates, valve boxes, engineering castings to drawing, ductile iron pipe fittings, Cambridge rings and other agricultural castings.
Manhole covers and gratings in EN 124 load classes A15, B125, C250 and D400.
Annual production of about 10 million kg; customers in 20+ countries; 80+ skilled professionals.
Led by Kailash Pat Agarwala (Founder & Chairman) and Punit Agarwala (Director).
